title: Source record
description: One cited source: its citation data, where to find it, its archived copies and history, and the rights to use it. Stored as content/sources/<first letter of key, or _other>/<key>.yaml.

key.description: Citation key used in text as [@key]. Must equal the file name.

kind.description: court-rule: rules of any court, including local rules. intergovernmental-agreement: a compact or agreement between governments, such as a tribal-state gaming compact. journal: a periodical as a whole, cited as a place to search.

citation.description: Citation Style Language JSON item (https://docs.citationstyles.org/). Rendered into footnotes by citeproc. 'id' is filled from 'key' at build time.

original_link.description: Where the original is published, if online.

retrieved.description: Date the source was last consulted.

archives.description: Archived copies. At least one is expected for every web source.

file.description: A copy stored in the project's R2 bucket. Served publicly only when rights.redistribution is true.

storage_key.description: Object key of the stored copy in the project's R2 bucket.

checksum.description: SHA-256 hash of the stored file, in lowercase hexadecimal.

history.description: Changes to the web page or file at the source's address, from the Internet Archive and scheduled re-checks. Versions of the document itself (an amendment, a revised constitution, a new edition of a code) are recorded in content/documents/ instead, and the source names its version in document_version (decision record 0018).

document_version.description: When this source is one version of a document that changes over time (a compact, an amendment, a constitution, an edition of a code or court rules), the document history record and the version it is. The version names this source in turn; scripts/lint_records.py checks that the two agree (decision record 0018).

shares_link_with.description: Keys of other source records at the same address that are different documents, such as several statutes on one chapter page or a case that quotes a statute. Without it, two records at one address (ignoring the scheme, 'www.', a trailing slash or an index page) are treated as duplicates by scripts/lint_records.py.

citator.description: Negative-treatment check for cases and statutes (e.g. KeyCite).

courtlistener.description: The case as CourtListener (Free Law Project) files it, matched by citation, case name and year from CourtListener's quarterly bulk data by scripts/caselaw/check_case_citations.py. Later uses (links, the citation graph, parentheticals) start from the cluster number.

citation.description: The citation that matched, such as "436 U.S. 49".

case_name.description: The case name as CourtListener gives it.

release.description: Date of the bulk data release checked.

court_dates.description: A case's dates other than its decision (citation.issued), each as the official report or the court's own record prints it: the U.S. Reports or the Court's own prints and docket for the Supreme Court, the reporter's head matter or the court's slip opinion for other courts. A date the source does not print is left out, never taken from secondary sources. The case box shows each date on its own line in order, with the decision among them (site/src/lib/server/case-facts.ts, pdf/pipeline/typst-writer.mjs). Checked by hand; the review is in research/reviews/2026-11-23-court-dates.csv.

argued.description: Oral argument, every day the source names.

argued_and_submitted.description: Argued and submitted for decision the same day, as the Ninth Circuit and others print it.

heard.description: Heard, as the First Circuit prints the day of argument.

submitted.description: Submitted for decision without argument, or on the briefs.

filed.description: Only when the opinion was filed on a different day from the decision, such as a district court opinion signed one day and filed the next.

printed.description: The dates exactly as the source prints them, to check against.

source.description: The official report, court print, docket or reporter head matter the dates come from.

note.description: Where other sources give a different date, and why this one is used.

caption.description: A case's caption as the official report prints it, naming the parties and their roles ("Samuel A. Worcester, Plaintiff in Error v. The State of Georgia"). Shown under Parties and nations on the case's page (site/src/lib/server/case-pages.ts). Letter case may be changed from small capitals; the words may not.

source.description: The official report or court print the caption comes from.

opinions.description: Each opinion in a case and the page of the official report where it starts, read from the report itself. The case's page lists them, each linked to its first page in the saved copy of the official report, and says which opinion each quotation comes from (site/src/lib/case-opinions.ts). Checked by hand.

source.description: The official report the pages come from.

justice.description: The writer, as the record's supreme_court.justices names them, or the judge's name for other courts. "The Court" for a per curiam opinion.

page.description: The report page where the opinion starts.

note.description: Anything a reader should know, such as an opinion the report does not print in full.

reading_links.description: Other places a reader can read this case or law, found and checked by scripts/caselaw/reading_links.py from the settings in research/reading-links/sites.yaml. The website shows them beside the citation.

access.description: official: the government's own text; free; subscription: needs an account, such as Westlaw or Lexis; background: not legal authority, such as Wikipedia.

unchecked.description: The site turns away automated checks, so the link follows the site's own stable address pattern without a check.

supreme_court.description: Who decided a Supreme Court case: the Court (named for the Chief Justice), the bench, the vote and each justice's part. From Oyez's public case data (scripts/law/supreme_court_benches.py), or from the official report where Oyez has none.

court.description: The Court named for its Chief Justice, such as "Warren Court".

natural_court.description: The bench that heard the case, as Oyez names it, such as "Warren Court (1958-1962)".

opinion.description: The opinion the justice wrote: majority, concurrence, dissent and the like.

source.description: The Oyez case, or the official report when Oyez has no vote data.

note.description: What the source does not settle, such as votes the report does not state.

contribution.description: For a source that reached the project from a person (an interview, a told story, a family document) rather than from publication: the public-safe summary of its contribution filing. Signed forms, recordings and contact details stay in the private filing (docs/contributions.md). When the contributor statement grants use, rights.status is 'granted' with basis 'permission'.

tribes.description: Tribe profile ids this source concerns.

nations_in_case.description: For a court case: each Native nation or people the case names, as a party or as what the case is about, matched to its nation record. 'tribes' lists the same nation ids. A name that does not match one nation today is listed under not_linked with the reason, rather than guessed.

checked.description: When the names were checked against the opinion.

named_as.description: The name the case gives, which may be a former name, an older spelling, a reservation or a historical nation.

role.description: party: the nation itself is a party (plaintiff, defendant, petitioner, respondent or intervenor). government: its officials, council, court, agency or business arm is a party. subject: the case concerns the nation, its land, its court or its members, but the nation is not a party.

historical.description: True when the case names a historical nation or band whose people are today part of the linked nation, or of several nations.

jurisdictions.description: The governments or legal orders the source concerns.

methods.description: Dispute resolution methods the source establishes, describes or analyzes. Add a method record with status 'proposed' for any process that has none.

topics.description: Free tags for grouping in bibliographies, e.g. history, treatise, court-connected-program, full-faith-and-credit. Not a fixed list.

annotation.description: Markdown. The annotated-bibliography entry: what the source is and why it matters to the project. Quotations carry pinpoints; the project's own judgments are labeled (project analysis).

access.description: How to reach the full text, so a researcher knows what needs a subscription database or a library.

open.description: True when the full text is free to read online.

note.description: What to pull and how, e.g. the annotated code section to open in Westlaw.

found_in.description: Research session ids (file names without .md) that found or updated this source.

courtDays.description: Days in order, YYYY-MM-DD; several when the source names several, such as argument over three days.
